name: 01_testConnection_success
description: Sync action `testConnection` against a valid personal token — expects a 200 on GET /outlets.

name: 02_testConnection_auth_failure
description: Sync action `testConnection` with an invalid personal token — expects a 401 and a failure payload. NOTE: record this test WITHOUT the shared secrets.json (or with a secrets file that omits '#personal_token') so the deliberately-invalid token below is not overwritten by the real one.

name: 03_sales_first_run
description: No input state -> after=0, full history. Produces `sales` + 4 child tables (design spec §7).

name: 04_sales_incremental
description: Seeded in/state.json {"last_version": N} -> asserts `after=N` request and advanced `last_version` in output state. NOTE: after recording 03_sales_first_run, copy its out/state.json last_version into this test's in/state.json before re-recording (or record independently against a store that has changed since the first-run cutoff).

name: 06_inventory
description: Happy path for `inventory` (composite product_id+outlet_id PK, no child tables).

name: 07_customers
description: Happy path for `customers`. Cassette response bodies get PII field names (email, phone, first_name, ...) scrubbed by the component's BodyFieldSanitizer.

name: 08_outlets
description: Happy path for `outlets` — a cheap, small reference stream. Good candidate to record first.

name: 09_registers
description: Happy path for `registers` — a cheap, small reference stream. Good candidate to record first.

name: 10_payment_types
description: Happy path for `payment_types` — a cheap, small reference stream.

name: 11_auth_failure
description: `run` action (not just the sync action) against an invalid token on the cheap `outlets` object -> expects exit 1. NOTE: same recording caveat as 02_testConnection_auth_failure — do not let the shared secrets.json's real token overwrite the deliberately-invalid one below.

name: 12_rate_limit_retry
description: A 429 (with a near-future RFC1123 Retry-After date) then 200 -> asserts the client waits and completes. NOTE: real stores rarely 429 on demand — after an initial live recording of a normal successful call, hand-edit the recorded cassette's first response to a 429 with a `Retry-After` header a few seconds in the future (not a fabricated body — same real request/response pair, edited status+headers) and keep the following real 200 response as-is.

name: 13_empty_first_page
description: `data: []` on the very first page -> zero rows, no crash, state unchanged/graceful. Record against an object/store combination that genuinely has zero rows (e.g. `payment_types` on a fresh trial store before any custom payment type is added), or set a very high `after` cursor via in/state.json so nothing new is returned.
